review_defects.where: apps/Model Plane/rust/services/execution-core/src/capability_policy.rs:575-589 (binding_for) and :1040 (version_accepts treats any registry binding as enforced under Shadow); reached through runtime_loop/mod.rs:834-835 execute_mcp
review_defects.scenario: TOOL_CLASS_GATE=shadow is supposed to be observe-only ("legacy decides"), and the plan flips it on in compose once S3 is proven. For an mcp__ name, though, shadow turns the legacy answer (always deny: no governed binding) into a live allow. Take an org that has an approved MCP tool row. merged_tool_defs (agent.rs:970-971) already offers every gateway-listed MCP tool, and RunAgentRequest.tools can add any mcp__ name. execution-core has MODEL_GATEWAY_ADDR set in compose. With shadow on, binding_for resolves the name from ResolveToolBindings, and capability-core allows a read-class tool (risk low). The permission engine returns Allow for mcp__ under Auto, and check_autonomy_rung passes when the rung is Unspecified. execute_mcp then calls ProxyMcpTool with expected_digest empty (mcp_gateway.rs:93), so the gateway skips its digest check. A high-risk MCP write becomes ask, and an approval then releases it and it runs. All of this happens before S4's MCP_DO_TOOLS gate (code default off, read on the proof stack, writes withheld per DEC-12), the class-driven permission engine and the expected_digest wiring exist. The digest the verifier checks is never bound to the call that is actually dispatched, so a server that changed the definition after the last observation runs under the old decision.
review_defects.fix: Make shadow observe-only for dynamic tools as well. Under Shadow, resolve and verify the mcp__ binding and count any divergence, but keep refusing with the legacy permission_denied ("tool has no governed capability binding"). Only Enforce, or S4's MCP_DO_TOOLS together with expected_digest passed to proxy_tool, should make an mcp__ name dispatchable. Add a test that a registered, approved mcp__ tool under Shadow still returns permission_denied.

review_defects.where: apps/Model Plane/go/services/capability-core/internal/server/server.go:520 (policy.Decide(result, binding) with binding == nil) and :608 evaluatedClass; verifier apps/Model Plane/rust/services/execution-core/src/capability_policy.rs:1094-1139 v2_mismatch
review_defects.scenario: When tool_name is named but no binding is found, the response and the signed claims carry the capability ceiling's class and floor, but Decide(result, nil) returns the risk-level result unchanged. That happens whenever WithToolBindingDatabase is not attached, which is the state of this tree until the lead applies the pending main.go edit, and also for a name that has no capability_tools row. Example: shadow or enforce, tool tickets.create. cap.tool.ticket.create is medium risk with an owner_effect/durable_owner ceiling. capability-core signs v2 {decision: allow, side_effect_class: owner_effect, approval_floor: durable_owner}. read_subagent_result (cap.agent.lineage.read, low risk, ceiling floor ask) is signed {allow, floor ask} in the same way. With the DB attached, both are ask. The execution-core verifier only checks that the vocabulary is consistent, never that an allow is compatible with its floor, so it accepts a signed decision that contradicts itself even under enforce. The slice's guarantee that a floor of ask or above becomes ask therefore depends on deployment wiring. Today only the separate permission-engine pause stops these calls, and S4/WS13 consumers of the signed floor would trust a self-contradictory allow.
review_defects.fix: When a tool is named and no binding is found, apply Decide with a synthetic binding built from the capability ceiling (class and floor) so the ceiling's floor tightens the decision. In v2_mismatch, refuse any allow whose signed approval_floor ranks at ask or above. Add an engine/server test for a named built-in tool with no DB handle.

review_defects.where: apps/Model Plane/go/services/capability-core/internal/server/server.go EvaluatePolicy tool binding branch (after lookupToolBinding)
review_defects.scenario: A built-in (non-mcp__) tool name that the registry binds to capability Z, evaluated under a different capability Y, falls back to Y's ceiling. capability-core then signs a v2 allow claiming tool X under capability Y with Y's class, for example tool_name=shell under cap.tool.http (read), signed allow. Any service principal with capability:read can mint this. execution-core rejects it today only because its static map pins the capability id. The signed claim does not establish a registry-owned binding, which is what v2 is supposed to guarantee.
review_defects.fix: When tool_name is not bound under the evaluated capability, deny with tool_not_bound if the name resolves under any other capability (or exists in capability_tools at all). Fall back to the ceiling only for a name the registry does not hold anywhere.

review_defects.where: apps/Model Plane/rust/services/execution-core/src/capability_policy.rs:794-810 (BindingState::table LRU eviction) with pin at :862
review_defects.scenario: The per-run pin of (version, class) lives in a 1024-run LRU, and every allowed call under shadow or enforce touches it, built-in tools included. On a busy replica, or with a tenant starting many short runs, an idle long-running run gets evicted. Its pins and binding table are dropped, so a later call re-resolves and re-pins whatever version the registry holds now. The guarantee that a mid-run version or class change fails closed silently lapses. A drifted digest is still denied by Decide, so this only affects a re-approval or reclassification mid-run.
review_defects.fix: Treat a pin lookup on a run that was evicted as unknown-and-failed-closed for dynamic tools (for example, keep a separate bounded set of evicted keys), or size the LRU by active runs and record evictions in a metric. Document the per-process, best-effort scope in the decision ledger.

review_defects.scenario: The plan row says to roll capability-core before execution-core. It also lets a continuation that fails right after its seeded round publish a zero-token ledger row, because the gateway guard is only `inference_rounds == 0` (money/audit). Fix: skip `record` when `first_of_segment` (the round was seeded), or make `first_of_segment` visible at the record site. review_defects.where: apps/Model Plane/rust/services/model-gateway/src/sse.rs agentic_run_stream: publish_agent_usage is called only after `let response = match dispatch_result` (~L10438-10457). follow_agentic_run (~L9793-9813) returns Err(DeadlineExpired) and drops (detaches) the dispatch JoinHandle.
review_defects.scenario: An unpinned Do run gets a 120 s follow deadline by default (AGENTIC_RUN_DEADLINE_DEFAULT_SECS; 270 s when pinned). execution-core has no wall clock by default (EXECUTION_RUN_WALL_CLOCK_SECS unset means off). Suppose a run takes longer than that: a long research task, many tool rounds, or subagents. The DeadlineExpired arm sends agent_dispatch_unknown and returns. The detached task keeps running, and execution-core finishes the run and returns a RunAgentResponse carrying the full RunUsage, but nothing reads it, so no AGENT_USAGE envelope is ever published. The same happens on the join-error arm. The longest and most expensive Do runs never reach the ledger, and any user can trigger this on purpose by asking for long work. That breaks the slice's own guarantee that Do-round usage reaches the ledger.
review_defects.fix: Publish inside the dispatch task itself: wrap the future that spawn_run_dispatch spawns so it calls publish_agent_usage as soon as RunAgent returns Ok, whether or not the follower is still waiting. Or give that task what it needs to publish. Keep the {request_id}-AGENT_USAGE key so the follower can never publish a second copy, and add a test where the deadline expires before the response arrives and the envelope is still published.

review_defects.where: apps/Model Plane/rust/services/execution-core/src/runtime_loop/agent.rs run_rounds: ctx.usage.record(&response) (~L2591) runs before the route guard and overwrites provider_used/model_used. sse.rs build_agent_usage_envelope: CostBasis::of_route(..).served_by(&usage.provider_used).
review_defects.scenario: Take a run pinned to the ChatGPT subscription. Rounds 1-3 are served by the subscription provider. Round 4 comes back from a metered provider (for example a stale or misconfigured inference-core falling back to 'openai'). The route guard refuses that round and the run ends RouteUnavailable, but the tally has already set provider_used to 'openai' and model_used to the substituted model. served_by() returns Metered when the provider is not a subscription provider, so it overrides the route's Subscription basis. The single envelope then has cost_basis 'metered' and the substituted model, and cost-core prices the tokens of all four rounds at API list price and enqueues billing. The subscription rounds get list-priced, which the plan forbids ('subscription never list-priced').
review_defects.fix: Do not let a round the route guard rejects decide the route or basis of the whole tally. Either record it after the guard passes, or keep a separate leg for wrong-route rounds, or never let a pinned route's basis be downgraded. Better still, carry the basis per leg, or at least make the envelope keep Subscription whenever the route is pinned. Add a test: three subscription rounds, then one wrong-provider round, must not produce cost_basis 'metered' for the summed tokens.

review_defects.where: apps/Model Plane/rust/services/execution-core/src/runtime_loop/agent.rs run_agent_with_route_parkable: `run_rounds(...).await?` (~L1469) and `finalize(...).await?` (~L1518-1533); UsageTally lives only in the Ok response.
review_defects.scenario: Rounds have already been spent (tokens charged by the provider) when run_rounds propagates a tonic::Status through `?`, for example a pause_for_approval or session write failure, or when finalize returns Err because the durable receipt write failed. The gateway then gets Ok(Ok(Err(status))) and takes the ambiguous or rejection arm, and the tally is dropped. Nothing is published for rounds the provider billed. A crash or receipt outage at the worst moment means spent inference that never reaches the ledger.
review_defects.fix: Report usage on the error path as well, for example in a status detail or trailer the gateway reads before it classifies the failure. Or document this as a known gap and have the ledger reconciled from execution-core's per-round logs, so the loss is visible rather than silent.

review_defects.where: apps/Model Plane/rust/services/execution-core/src/runtime_loop/agent.rs UsageTally::record (provider_used/model_used = last counted round) + sse.rs build_agent_usage_envelope (one envelope, one model)
review_defects.scenario: An unpinned run's rounds (or its delegates' rounds) can be served by different providers or models, for example when inference-core falls back to another provider partway through the run. All tokens are summed into one envelope priced at the LAST round's model. Suppose early rounds ran on an expensive model and the last on a cheap fallback, or the other way round: the bill is wrong in either direction. review_defects.fix: Tally per (provider, model), as a repeated leg in RunUsage, and publish one envelope per leg with a key like {request_id}-AGENT_USAGE-{n}. Or refuse to price a mixed tally under a single model.

notes: Fix for the review finding (high). Previously the follower published the usage envelope after it received the RunAgentResponse. When the follow deadline expired (120 s unpinned, 270 s pinned) or the join failed, the dispatch task was detached and its tally was dropped, so long runs never reached the ledger. Now the dispatch task publishes the envelope itself. In sse.rs, publish_agent_usage is replaced by a private AgentUsageLedger struct, which owns an Arc of the publisher plus the switch value, ids, model, zdr, route, privacy tier and start instant. Its publish method keeps the same guards as before: switch strictly 'true', not zdr, inference_rounds > 0. spawn_run_dispatch takes the ledger as a new last parameter. Inside the spawned task, right after run_agent returns Ok with usage set, it calls ledger.publish, whether or not the follower is still waiting. The follower's publish block in agentic_run_stream is removed, so the {request_id}-AGENT_USAGE key can only be published from the task and never twice. The ledger is built at the call site, with the switch read from the environment at dispatch time. Paused and parked responses are still billed, because the task publishes on every Ok response. Tests: the e2e FollowedTurn gained a publisher field. The new e2e test sets a 1 s deadline and a 3 s executor delay. It asserts the stream ended with agent_dispatch_unavailable and no envelope yet, then polls the publisher and asserts exactly one USAGE_ENVELOPE with the -AGENT_USAGE key, run_id and the summed tokens and cache read. The sse.rs unit helper now uses AgentUsageLedger, and the latency assertion became is_u64 because latency is now measured from the stored start instant.
